title: Which property lets us add the term values in any order?
description: An expression with a curved line group, a product and a single number is split into terms, each term is worked out, and the values are added in two different orders. The two properties of addition are named. Keeko doubts the first term and ignores the curved lines.
teaching_notes: One idea: the values of the terms can be added in any order, because addition is commutative and associative. Watch for children who ignore the curved lines and multiply before adding inside them.

source: Evaluate 5 × (3 + 2) + 7 × 8 + 3 by terms, and name the property that lets you add the term values in any order.
video_script.why: The child sees why the values of terms can be added in any order and learns the names of the two properties.
video_script.substitution: List the terms, work out each term, add the values in two different orders, and name the properties.
video_script.anchor: An expression with three terms: five times the sum of three and two, seven times eight, and three
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko ignores the curved lines and reads the first term as five times three, then plus two, so the first term becomes seventeen instead of twenty five.

final_answer.spoken: the value is eighty four, in every order of adding

never_show: 17 as the value of the first term
maths_rules: slip: 5 × 3 + 2 = 17, which ignores the curved lines
video_script.design: One idea: term values can be added in any order, by the commutative and associative properties. Assumes terms, products and sums inside curved lines. Wrong idea: ignore the curved lines. The expression stays on the board all video.

narration: <bookmark mark='book'/>This is a question from your book.
<bookmark mark='expr'/>Look at five times the sum of three and two, plus seven times eight, plus three.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>Which parts are added, what is the value, and why can we add them in any order?

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

narration: <bookmark mark='think'/>Think and tell.

beats.on_screen: 2 + 3 = 3 + 2 with the label commutative property; (2 + 3) + 4 = 2 + (3 + 4) with the label associative property

marks.comm: 2 + 3 = 3 + 2 appears and the label commutative property lands on it
marks.assoc: (2 + 3) + 4 = 2 + (3 + 4) appears and the label associative property lands on it

narration: <bookmark mark='comm'/>Swapping terms does not change the sum, and this is called the commutative property of addition.
<bookmark mark='assoc'/>Grouping does not change the sum, and this is called the associative property of addition.
<bookmark mark='given'/>Given, the expression five times the sum of three and two, plus seven times eight, plus three.

beats.on_screen: To find: the terms, the value, and the property that allows any order

marks.find: the words terms, value and property are written

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to list the terms, find the value, and name the property that allows any order.

marks.first: 5 × (3 + 2) is marked as the first term
marks.rest: 7 × 8 and 3 are marked as the second and third terms

narration: <bookmark mark='first'/>Step one, list the terms. The first term is five times the sum of three and two.
<bookmark mark='rest'/>The second term is seven times eight, and the third term is three.

marks.two: 7 × 8 is worked out as 56 and the last term stays 3

narration: <bookmark mark='one'/>Step two, find the value of each term. Three plus two is five, and five times five is twenty five.
<bookmark mark='two'/>Seven times eight is fifty six, and the last term is three.
<bookmark mark='add'/>Step three, add the values in order. Twenty five plus fifty six is eighty one.
<bookmark mark='last'/>Then we add the last term, three.
<bookmark mark='other'/>Step four, add the same values in another order. Three plus fifty six is fifty nine.
<bookmark mark='last'/>Then we add twenty five to fifty nine.

beats.on_screen: Answer: 84 in every order; commutative property and associative property

marks.ans: both orders end in 84 and the answer is boxed
marks.names: the labels commutative property and associative property glow

narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>The value is eighty four in both orders.
<bookmark mark='names'/>We can add in any order because of the commutative property and the associative property of addition.
<bookmark mark='hand'/>Keeko has raised a hand. Let us check the doubt and solve it.

beats.on_screen: Keeko's bubble shows 5 × 3 + 2 = 17; beside it 5 × (3 + 2) with the curved lines glowing; the bubble is struck through in the warning colour

marks.fix: the curved lines glow and the bubble is struck through

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko reads the first term as five times three plus two. That gives seventeen, and the curved lines are ignored.
<bookmark mark='fix'/>But the curved lines tell us to add three and two first. Then five times five is twenty five.
